title: Strange Printer
spaceBreakdown:
- vector<vector<int>> dp: n × n entries → O(n^2)
- recursion depth: none (iterative)
- not counted: input string s
approach: The key insight is that when two positions k and j (k < j) hold the same character, they can be printed in a single turn: print s[k] over the entire range [k, j] (covering the interior), then separately print the interior [k+1, j-1]. This yields the recurrence dp[i][j] = min(dp[i][j-1] + 1, min over k in [i, j-1] with s[k]==s[j] of dp[i][k] + dp[k+1][j-1]). We fill the table by increasing interval length so all subproblems are ready.
hints: For a substring s[i..j], if some earlier position k has s[k] == s[j], what does printing that character once across [k, j] let you reuse for the two pieces on either side of the interior?
Use interval dynamic programming: dp[i][j] = minimum turns for s[i..j]. For "aba", dp[0][2] takes dp[0][1]+1 = 3, but since s[0]=='a'==s[2], try dp[0][0] + dp[1][1] = 2.

**Single character** - only one turn is needed
`Input: "a"` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: skipping the L==1 base case and reading dp[i][j-1] for j-1 < i → returns 0

**All same characters** - every position shares one turn
`Input: "aaaa"` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: using dp[i][j] = dp[i][j-1] + 1 with no merge check → returns 4

**Palindrome with matching endpoints** - endpoints merge, middle is separate
`Input: "aba"` → `Expected: 2`
⚠️ Bug: checking only k = j-1 for the merge instead of all k in [i, j-1] → returns 3

**All distinct characters** - no merges possible
`Input: "abc"` → `Expected: 3`
⚠️ Bug: initialising dp[i][j] to 0 instead of dp[i][j-1]+1 → returns 0

followUps.q: What if the printer could print non-contiguous positions in one turn?
followUps.a: Then each distinct character needs exactly one turn, since all its positions print together. The answer is the number of distinct characters, computable in O(n) time and O(1) space.

followUps.q: What if s.length could be up to 10^4?
followUps.a: First compress runs of identical consecutive characters into one (they never add turns), shrinking n. Then run the same interval DP; worst case (alternating characters) stays O(n^3), but typical inputs shrink dramatically.

followUps.q: What if you must also output the actual sequence of print operations?
followUps.a: Store the optimal split index k alongside each dp[i][j] entry, then backtrack from dp[0][n-1] recursively, emitting a print of s[j] over [k, j] whenever a merge was used. Same O(n^3) time, O(n^2) extra space for the split table.
